I am 62 years old, been farming these 10.9 mu for 40 years since my father handed them over. I only finished primary school, but I know this land better than any book. My wheat-maize land is 8 mu, and I keep 2.9 mu for cotton. Last year the wheat did about 1000 jin per mu, and the maize did around 1100 jin. This year I will do the same — no reason to change what works. My son works in Shijiazhuang and sends some money home, so I have a little to spend on inputs, but every yuan matters. I would rather put a bit too much fertilizer than risk a bad harvest. A bad harvest is a disaster; wasting some fertilizer is just a cost.

For wheat, I plant Jimai 22, same as Old Wang next door. It is an improved variety, not those fancy new ones I do not trust yet. After the maize comes off, I rotary till the field. For fertilizer, I put one 50-jin bag of compound fertilizer — the 15-15-15 kind from the dealer — on each mu as base, and then top-dress with another 40 jin of urea at green-up time. That is about 25 kg of nitrogen per mu, 8 kg of phosphate, and 7 kg of potassium. I irrigate three times: winter water, jointing stage, and grain filling. I spray three times total — herbicide once, then insecticide twice when I see aphids. I expect 500 kg per mu, same as last year if the weather holds.

For maize, I plant Denghai 605, hybrid seed. Everyone around here uses it now because it stands up better. After wheat harvest in June, I no-till plant straight into the stubble — no time to waste, the summer season is short. I spread about 80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, which gives around 16 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphate, and 6 kg potassium. I do not put as much nitrogen as wheat because the wheat field already had fertilizer in it. Two irrigations: one at the big trumpet stage, one at filling. Three pesticide sprays total. I expect 550 kg per mu.

For cotton, I have 2.9 mu of Guoxinmian. Cotton needs more work and more watching. I rotary till in spring, put one bag of compound fertilizer and some urea on it — about 18 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphate, and 8 kg potassium per mu. The cotton bollworm is the real problem in July and August. I spray about every 10 days in summer, 10 times total. Two irrigations, one at flowering and one at boll stage. I expect about 275 kg per mu of seed cotton. I keep the cotton plot small because my wife and I cannot manage more with just the two of us at home — the children are all working outside.

Fertilizer prices are still high this year, but I have some savings from my son. I will not cut back. Last year my nephew cut his wheat fertilizer to save money and his wheat was stunted. Not worth the risk.
